claim: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite connected simple graph with \(d=|V|\ge3\), make every vertex a boundary vertex, replace every edge by an interval of common length \(\ell>0\), and let \(\Lambda_G(\lambda)\) be the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for \(-u''=\lambda u\). For an odd integer \(n\ge1\), put \(\lambda_0=(n\pi/\ell)^2\) and define the sharp local pole coefficient \[C_*(G)=\lim_{\lambda\to\lambda_0,\ \lambda\ne\lambda_0}|\lambda-\lambda_0|\,\sigma_{\min}(\Lambda_G(\lambda)).\]If \(Q(G)=D(G)+A(G)\) is the signless Laplacian and \(q_{\min}(G)\) its least eigenvalue, then \[C_*(G)=\frac{2\lambda_0}{\ell}\,q_{\min}(G).\]Hence \(C_*(G)>0\) exactly when \(G\) is non-bipartite. Among all simple \(d\)-vertex all-boundary equilateral decorations, the complete graph \(K_d\) uniquely maximizes the pole coefficient, with \[C_*(K_d)=\frac{2\lambda_0}{\ell}(d-2).\]At an even Dirichlet resonance the corresponding coefficient is \(0\). For the four-boundary triangle-with-one-pendant-edge resonator used as the degree-four example by Do--Kuchment--Ong, \(q_{\min}=(5-\sqrt{17})/2\), so \(K_4\) improves the sharp pole coefficient by the exact factor \((5+\sqrt{17})/2\).

integrity.computational_dependence: none for the proof; finite enumeration and resonance checks are supplementary
integrity.novelty_scope: Exact signless-Laplacian reduction of the resonant pole coefficient and unique complete-graph optimizer within the all-boundary equilateral simple-graph class.
integrity.prior_work_preserved: The general resonant gap mechanism, the existence estimate, and the odd-cycle construction are credited to Do--Kuchment--Ong; standard signless-Laplacian bipartiteness facts are credited to graph-spectral literature.

scientific_limitations: The optimized quantity is the local Dirichlet-to-Neumann pole coefficient, not a host-independent exact spectral-gap width.
The optimization is restricted to finite connected simple all-boundary equilateral decorations with fixed vertex count and common edge length.
Internal vertices, unequal lengths, potentials, magnetic phases, multiple edges, and generalized vertex conditions are outside the theorem.
An equivalent formula may exist under M-function or boundary-triple terminology in literature not surfaced by the searches.
title: Signless-Laplacian pole strength and optimal equilateral quantum-graph resonators
